subject: Clarify incident notification timelines & EU evidence handoff
messages:
From: Claudia Foster <claudia.foster@brightbank.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: security@brightbank.com, BrightBank Legal <legal@brightbank.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident notification & evidence handoff — clarifying timelines for EU customers

Hi Olga / Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks for taking this on. Our privacy team is reviewing the DPA and has a couple of specific asks we need clarified before we proceed with onboarding:

- Notification timeline: Our SLO requires notification of any security incident affecting EU personal data within 72 hours of detection. Please confirm Redwood's contractual notification window and whether you can commit to the same 72-hour obligation for EU-resident data.
- Evidence handoff: If we request forensic snapshots or exports (for EU subjects), we need a documented chain-of-custody and an initial handoff within 14 days, with an interim triage packet within 72 hours. Can Redwood commit to a 14-day evidence delivery window for exports that require cross-border transfer approvals?
- Jurisdictional consent / data flows: Are there any subprocessors or export paths that would require BrightBank to obtain additional consents for EU transfers? We need a roster of subprocessors and the locations where exports may be staged.

Attached is our security questionnaire (Q3) and the redlines our legal team is proposing as an addendum to the DPA. If you can confirm the above and indicate what evidence you can realistically provide in the 72-hour triage packet vs the 14-day handoff, we can prepare the DocuSign addendum and schedule a short call.

Thanks — Claudia

Subject: Re: Incident notification & evidence handoff — clarifying timelines for EU customers

Hi Claudia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and a proposed path forward below.

1) Notification window
We contractually support 72-hour notification for incidents that meet Redwood's incident criteria and materially affect customer data. Practically, our SOC/Rapid Response team will aim to issue an initial incident notification (triage) within 48–72 hours of detection with an internal severity assessment and next steps. We can mirror your 72-hour ask in the DPA addendum — Gartner-style language around "reasonable efforts to notify" with an explicit 72-hour target is fine.

2) Evidence handoff timelines
- Triage packet (within 72 hours): we can provide a snapshot report (timeline, affected services, high-level indicators), logs meta-data, and a list of accounts/IDs potentially impacted.
- Full forensic export (14-day box): we can aim for a 14-day delivery for requested forensic exports, subject to legal review and export controls for EU personal data. We will produce a chain-of-custody manifest and provide an encrypted transfer mechanism (SFTP / secure share). If the export requires a cross-border transfer that triggers additional controls, we will notify you immediately and propose a mitigated timeframe — but our target remains 14 days for standard cases.

3) Subprocessors & export staging
Please see the attached redwood_subproc_roster.pdf — it lists current subprocessors and the primary processing regions. For EU-resident data, most exports are staged in EU or in our EU partner region; a small subset (for forensic toolchains) may be processed in a redacted/controlled environment in the US. If BrightBank requires EU-only processing for exports, we can evaluate options (on-prem escrow, dedicated EU-only ingest) but that will affect timelines and cost.

Next steps
- I can join a legal + security call later this week to walk through the questionnaire and proposed DPA addendum language.
- Ben, can you prepare a short note on our encrypted transfer and chain-of-custody process?

Olga

Subject: Re: Incident notification & evidence handoff — clarifying timelines for EU customers

Thanks Olga — that addresses most of our questions. A couple of clarifications: 

- The 72-hour triage packet needs to include at minimum: incident detection timestamp (UTC), list of affected tenant IDs, a summary of the data classes affected (PII / non-PII), and whether any exports or third-party transfers occurred.
- For the 14-day handoff we require: (a) a manifest of included files and hash values, (b) the chain-of-custody PDF signed by Redwood's forensic lead, and (c) a documented transfer method with supporting logs.
- Our legal team prefers explicit DPA addendum language stating Redwood will make "commercially reasonable efforts" to provide the 72-hour packet and a 14-day handoff for EU-resident data, and to identify any export paths that would require additional consents.

We've uploaded the proposed addendum to DocuSign — link below — and our legal contact (M. Hargreaves) will join the call if needed. Can we lock a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00 AM BST?

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/brightbank/dpa-addendum-12345

Best,
Claudia

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Olga / Kimberly — quick internal note before the call with BrightBank at 10:00 BST tomorrow. Summary of asks and owner/risks: 

- Customer asks: 72-hour triage packet + 14-day forensic export with chain-of-custody and hashes; explicit DPA addendum language re: commercially reasonable efforts and export-path disclosure. (Owner: Olga)
- Technical deliverables: produce triage packet template (48–72hr), chain-of-custody PDF template, and SFTP/export playbook. (Owner: Ben / Infra Sec)
- Legal: review the proposed DocuSign addendum and approve the "commercially reasonable efforts" phrasing (Owner: Kimberly)
- Risk flags: if BrightBank insists on EU-only forensic handling for all exports, we need to flag potential timeline/cost impact and discuss dedicated EU-only deployment options.

Immediate asks for the call:
1) Olga — confirm what will be included in the triage packet (we can reuse existing incident templates but add tenant ID list and data-class summary).
2) Kimberly — be prepared to speak to the DPA addendum phrasing; if legal wants tighter guarantees we should surface the commercial ops impact.
3) Infra — confirm encryption / transfer options and whether we can provide pre-signed transfer logs on a 14-day cadence.

I'll be on the call and will take notes.

Thanks — Ben
